title: Infleqtion Sqale: 30 entangled logical qubits on 80 neutral atoms (10 x [[8,3,2]], error detection with post-selection), IQP circuit with 4 logical CCZ gates
summary: Infleqtion press release (8-K Ex. 99.1, 2026-09-24) and technical write-up by CTO Pranav Gokhale (same date). 80 atoms in 10 blocks of 8 encode 30 logical qubits. Each block is prepared in the |000> state of the distance-3 [[8,3,3]] code, and the experiments themselves use the distance-2 [[8,3,2]] encoding. Handling is error detection with post-selection; a lost atom is reconstructed from parity constraints in post-processing. The benchmark is an IQP circuit entangling all 30 logical qubits: about 1,000 physical operations, 136 physical two-qubit gates and 4 transversal logical CCZ gates. Reported metric: a hit fraction of about 25% against a 0.024% uniform-random baseline (about 1,000x). No logical fidelity, acceptance rate, physical gate fidelity or mid-circuit measurement for this run. A full paper is promised 'in the coming weeks'.
error_correction_ratio: 8:3 (~2.67:1) with a distance-2 error-detecting code; not error correction

key_specs.circuit: IQP, 4 logical CCZ, ~1,000 physical ops, 136 physical 2q gates

actionable: Not a frontier. It is below Quantinuum's 94 error-detected logical qubits (Helios, Feb 2026) and QuEra/Harvard's 96 error-corrected (Jan 2026), and its 8:3 overhead comes from a distance-2 detection code, so it is not comparable to the knowledge base's error-correction ratio row. It counts as a demonstrated logical-qubit result only in the error-detected, post-selected sense, with vendor-only evidence so far. Re-check when the paper appears.
notes: Details were checked against Infleqtion's own write-up, not only press coverage. The comparison-to-baseline metric is the vendor's; no independent reproduction exists yet.
